data.title: Capri signals fiscal 2027 EPS of $2.20 on ~$3.42B revenue as Michael Kors targets return to growth in Q4
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Capri Holdings Limited (CPRI) Q2 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • "We are encouraged by the momentum build at both Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo" (Chairman & CEO John Idol), adding that "new fall product introductions are generating some of the strongest full price sell-throughs we have seen in years" and that management is "increasing our fiscal 2027 revenue and earnings per share guidance" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • "Revenue was impacted by approximately $50 million due to inventory delays, which constrained product availability" at Michael Kors (Chairman & CEO Idol), while the company continued to push "approximately 40% less markdown inventory" and "reduced promotional activity by approximately 50%" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • "Today, we have 7 Jet Set lounges" and "we have renovated 50 stores as we advance toward our goal of renovating 300 stores" (Chairman & CEO Idol), while also stating, "next year, we're going to open between 50 and 75 brand-new stores" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • "Second quarter revenue exceeded our expectations, increasing 11.5% over last year" at Jimmy Choo (Chairman & CEO Idol), and management said it "continue[s] to expect Jimmy Choo to return to profitability in fiscal 2027" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • "Total company revenue of $809 million decreased 5.5% on a reported basis" and "net income was $45 million or $0.42 per diluted share versus a loss per share of $0.03 last year" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Tyler Reddien).

Outlook

  • "We now anticipate fiscal 2027 revenue of approximately $3.42 billion" and "expect to generate diluted earnings per share of $2.20" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), while also raising the capital return assumption: "we now anticipate weighted average shares outstanding of approximately 108 million, reflecting share repurchases of $300 million during fiscal 2027" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • "Turning to third quarter guidance. We expect total company revenue of just over $1 billion" and "expect to generate diluted earnings per share of $0.95" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), noting the quarter includes "the impact of the $20 million of wholesale shipments that shifted from the third quarter into the second quarter" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • On what changed versus last quarter’s framing, management said the improved outlook was tied to in-quarter execution and brand momentum: "based on our second quarter performance and our expectations for the remainder of the year, we are increasing our fiscal 2027 revenue and earnings per share guidance" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

Financial Results

  • "Total company operating income of $31 million represented operating margin expansion of 150 basis points year-over-year to 3.8%" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), while "gross margin of 63.3% increased 230 basis points versus last year" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • By brand, "Michael Kors revenue of $663 million decreased 8.6%" while "Jimmy Choo. Revenue of $146 million increased 11.5%" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), with each brand benefiting from shipment timing: "around $15 million" for Michael Kors and "approximately $5 million" for Jimmy Choo shifting from Q3 into Q2 (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Balance sheet and buybacks were a key investment focus: "we ended the second quarter with cash of $125 million and debt of $461 million, resulting in net debt of $336 million, down from $1.6 billion last year" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), and "repurchasing $150 million worth of shares" including "10.3 million shares" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

Q&A

  • Matthew Boss, JPMorgan: "could you speak to the drivers of sequential month-over-month improvement" and "support your confidence for positive revenue growth in the back half"; Chairman & CEO Idol: "we were very pleased" and said the business is "literally chasing inventory on certain products" while emphasizing promotions were "down by 50%" and inventory was "$50 million less than we had planned" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • Brooke Roach, Goldman Sachs: asked about "Michael Kors Americas outlet" and "How quickly can you chase" winning products; Chairman & CEO Idol: outlet saw "slightly stronger acceleration" and on Hamilton Soft, "The sell-throughs, I would say, surprised us" and "we're moving as fast as we possibly can" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • Simeon Siegel, Guggenheim: asked the "right size" of wholesale and back-half gross margin drivers; Chairman & CEO Idol: "somewhere in the 20% range, 25% range" for wholesale mix and "we believe is going to return to growth next year" (Chairman & CEO Idol). Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien: "we are expecting that we'll see a bit of a pullback in the expansion" in 2H gross margin, citing tariffs and anniversarying prior benefits (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Adrienne Yih-Tennant, Barclays: asked about a "fashion shift" and whether customers are "new" vs "reactivated"; Chairman & CEO Idol: "we are definitely seeing the fashion winds shift" and said, "we're attracting new younger customers" and that TikTok Shop is "almost 4x from what we had originally anticipated" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • Rakesh Patel, Raymond James: asked about AUR durability as quality-of-sale moderates; Chairman & CEO Idol: "we've started to raise prices in outlet" and said more selective increases are planned because "they're not good enough. We have much higher aspirations" (Chairman & CEO Idol). Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien: "we do see significant opportunities in terms of gross margin expansion" beyond fiscal 2027 (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Mark Altschwager, Baird: asked whether Q3 assumes October trends hold and whether full-price turns positive; Chairman & CEO Idol: "there's absolutely a sequential improvement planned throughout the quarter" and "this does assume that Michael Kors full price does return to positive during the quarter" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and validation-seeking, anchored on inflection points and durability, including: "It is really nice to see the gross margin inflection" (Adrienne Yih-Tennant, Barclays) and "It is really nice to see the gross margin inflection" themes repeated across outlets and AUR questions.

  • Management’s tone was positive in prepared remarks and confident in Q&A, frequently reinforcing momentum signals such as "these are more than just green shoots" (Chairman & CEO Idol) and framing capital return as conviction: "This increase underscores our confidence" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Versus last quarter’s more cautious framing around "headwinds" and a "disappointed" Q2 outlook, management now leaned more assertively on recovery language, including "we are increasing our fiscal 2027 revenue and earnings per share guidance" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance moved up from "fiscal '27 revenue of approximately $3.4 billion" and EPS "approximately $2.15" (Q1 call, Chairman & CEO Idol) to "fiscal 2027 revenue of approximately $3.42 billion" and EPS "$2.20" (Q2 call, Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • The assumed repurchase level increased from "share repurchases of $200 million during fiscal 2027" (Q1 call, Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien) to "share repurchases of $300 million during fiscal 2027" (Q2 call, Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Operationally, Q1 emphasized "lower-than-anticipated inventory levels at Michael Kors in the second quarter" (Chairman & CEO Idol), while Q2 described improving flow and sell-throughs and said "the majority of these actions are now behind us" on quality-of-sale resets (Chairman & CEO Idol).

Risks and Concerns

  • Supply chain and availability remained a key risk: "Revenue was impacted by approximately $50 million due to inventory delays" (Chairman & CEO Idol), and management highlighted continued freight constraints: "issues with getting freight out of Asia" and "supplementing with air" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • Regional and macro risks were explicitly cited: EMEA was "impacted by the broader effects of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), while margins face pressure as "second half tariff rates on average will be a bit higher" and the company anniversaries "the tariff refund" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

Final Takeaway

Management characterized Q2 as a turning point where Michael Kors product newness and lower promotions drove improving monthly trends, while Jimmy Choo extended double-digit growth momentum. Leadership raised full-year guidance to approximately $3.42 billion in revenue and $2.20 in diluted EPS, paired with an increased $300 million share repurchase assumption, while continuing to flag inventory timing, tariffs, and Middle East-related demand pressures as the principal swing factors into the back half.

data.title: Reddit falls 29% to new 52-week low on weak Q4 guidance
data.description:
Reddit (RDDT) shares tumbled about 29% on Friday, closing at $91.73 after a drop of $37.87 on the day. The slide took the stock to a new 52-week low of $89.28.

The social platform reported third-quarter results that beat expectations but issued fourth-quarter guidance that came in below analyst consensus. 

Reddit reported Q3 revenue of $895 million, up 53% year over year, with GAAP EPS of $1.40. Despite those beats, management's Q4 revenue outlook of $1.0–$1.03 billion fell short of consensus, and warnings about deteriorating search-referral traffic sent shares sharply lower. data.title: Xponential Fitness jumps as investor looks to purchase Club Pilates owner (update)
data.description:
Update 4:48pm: Adds Fund 1 confirmation in filing.

Xponential Fitness (XPOF) soared 19% after Fund 1 Investments LLC, the third-largest holder,  said it was looking to buy the company,

Fund 1 is prepared to offer a price of $5.61 to $7 a share to purchase Xponential (XPOF), the owner of Club Pilates and Pure Barre brands,  according to a letter disclosed in a 13D/A filing on Friday.  At the top of the range, an offer would value XPOF at a premium of 87% to its closing price on Thursday.

Fund 1 owns almost 10% of Xponential's outstanding shares and has economic exposure to almost 20% of the company, according to the filing.

"While we are interested in acquiring 100% of the Company, we also are open to allowing other shareholders to participate in the acquisition alongside Fund 1, with Fund 1 acquiring the majority interest, so that they can take part in any upside," Fund 1 said in the letter to the Xponential board on Friday.

News of the offer was earlier reported by Bloomberg.

Xponential didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment from Bloomberg.

"Our interactions with the Board to date have been highly constructive, and we are grateful to you for that,"  Fund 1 wrote in the letter. "We came into this situation with an open mind and, given the governance challenges the Company has faced in the past, expected hurdles. Instead, we have been genuinely, positively surprised." 

In April, Xponential (XPOF), the franchisor of boutique fitness studios, announced that its board has initiated a review of strategic alternatives to maximize shareholder value.

data.title: MTX expects Q4 EPS of $1.15-$1.20 while targeting $100M incremental revenue from high-purity calcium in 3-5 years
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Minerals Technologies (MTX) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "This is a quarter that I would characterize with some significant highlights, solid top line growth for the company and a record operating performance in Engineered Solutions and also some challenges, dealing with another round of energy and raw material inflation in Consumer & Specialties." (Chairman & CEO Douglas Dietrich)

  • "We continued along our target growth track this quarter with sales of $555 million, up 4% over last year." (Chairman & CEO Dietrich)

  • "Our operating income in the third quarter was $72 million, and earnings per share were $1.53." (Chairman & CEO Dietrich)

  • "Our Engineered Solutions segment had another very strong quarter... generating 17.6% operating margins." (Chairman & CEO Dietrich)

  • "Total operating income for the company was slightly below our guidance this quarter, driven by a challenging operating quarter in Consumer & Specialties due to the significant increases in energy, transportation and raw material costs." (Chairman & CEO Dietrich)

  • "Year-to-date, our cash from operations is $171 million, up 32% compared to last year." (Chairman & CEO Dietrich)

  • "Lastly, we announced that we increased our regular quarterly dividend by 8% to $0.13 per share." (Chairman & CEO Dietrich)

  • "Earlier in October, we completed a private offering for $400 million of senior notes due in 2032... and expanded its capacity to $500 million." (Senior VP of Finance & Treasury and CFO Erik Aldag)

  • "We continue to see commercial adoption with 10 full-scale municipal drinking water installations." (Group President of Engineered Solutions Brett Argirakis)

Outlook

  • "Fourth quarter sales for MTI are expected to be approximately $525 million, with operating income between $60 million and $63 million and EPS between $1.15 and $1.20." (CFO Aldag)

  • "It's worth highlighting that there are 6 fewer days in our fourth quarter this year compared to last year." (CFO Aldag)

  • "We expect segment sales to decrease by approximately 10% sequentially, driven primarily by the typical seasonal reduction in project activity in the Environmental & Infrastructure product line." (CFO Aldag)

  • "We remain confident that the combination of price-cost recovery, volume leverage and the continued growth of higher-margin new products will contribute to higher margins in 2027." (CFO Aldag)

  • "We have good line of sight that our mid-single-digit top line growth will continue next year." (CFO Aldag)

Financial Results

  • "We continued along our target growth track this quarter with sales of $555 million." (Chairman & CEO Dietrich)

  • "Operating income for the quarter was $72 million." (CFO Aldag)

  • "Third quarter sales for the Consumer & Specialties segment were $278 million." (CFO Aldag)

  • "Operating income for the segment was $25 million in the third quarter." (CFO Aldag)

  • "In the third quarter... total sales of $277 million" for Engineered Solutions and "operating income for the segment was $49 million... and operating margin was very strong at 17.6%." (CFO Aldag)

  • "Cash from operations totaling $76 million, and free cash flow of $52 million." (CFO Aldag)

  • "Capital expenditures totaled $24 million in the third quarter, and we expect to be in the $95 million to $100 million range for the full year." (CFO Aldag)

  • "Net debt stood at $579 million, and our net leverage ratio decreased to 1.5x EBITDA." (CFO Aldag)

Q&A

  • Dan Moore, CJS Securities: "by sometime in Q1, you would expect to sort of catch up" on price-cost? CFO Aldag: "We're looking at another roughly $5 million of cost increases sequentially" in Q4 and, if costs stabilize, "you could see us at a company level at 14% in the second quarter of next year... getting back to that 14.5%, 15% run rate in the second half of next year."

  • Dan Moore, CJS Securities: cadence/capex for high-purity calcium and steel slag? Chairman & CEO Dietrich: high-purity calcium is "a nearer term" ramp, while steel slag will "probably pilot... mid next year"; and on calcium capex, "nothing outsized at this point" and "probably only be in the $5 million to $10 million kind of range" above average. Group President Argirakis: "we're working really closely... to assure that we can ramp up and meet the 2027 demand" and "we expect really to generate $100 million over the next 3 to 5 years." Group President D. J. Monagle: for steel slag, "make a decision on a pilot plant probably early next year" and the pilot plant "probably a $10 million to $15 million range."

  • Michael Harrison, Seaport Research Partners: Household & Personal Care demand/competition and Bleaching Earth/Fabric Care contribution? Group President Monagle: in pet care, "low single-digit sort of growth" with "E-commerce" higher; Bleaching Earth "got off to a little bit of a slow start" but is "pretty close to being at capacity"; Fabric Care is "probably a $20 million growth opportunity for us."

  • Michael Harrison, Seaport Research Partners: steel/refractories drivers (including data centers)? Group President Argirakis: U.S. steel demand "remains strong" and data centers are "about 2% of the steel production in the U.S. right now"; Europe is "a little sluggish" and "the Iran conflict continues to create some supply and export issues."

  • Michael Harrison, Seaport Research Partners: Environmental & Infrastructure growth/backlog into 2027? Chairman & CEO Dietrich: "I'm going to be hesitant to say that we're going to see 11%, 12%, 15% kind of growth" and tied uncertainty to "interest rates." Group President Argirakis: year-to-date "we're showing a 15% growth" with "Environmental Products revenue... up about 18%" and "drilling products... up over 20%."

  • Peter Osterland, Truist Securities: Q4 embedded H&PC growth and underperformers? CFO Aldag: "we're looking at probably mid to high single-digit growth for Household & Personal Care" and days-adjusted "probably close to double-digit growth." Chairman & CEO Dietrich: Fabric Care and Bleaching Earth had a "delay" but "that's over" and "that's starting to ramp nicely."

  • Peter Osterland, Truist Securities: Specialty Additives growth into 2027? Chairman & CEO Dietrich: "we think that... brings the Specialty Additives business to probably some growth, probably low single-digit growth." Group President Monagle: "we also have 2 new opportunities coming online" and "the pipeline is pretty robust."

  • David Silver, Prime Executions: PFAS commercialization pace and integration issues? Group President Argirakis: PFAS is "still in its early stages"; "another 10 that are scheduled for next year" and "8 additional systems that have been specified"; plus pilots and projects across "the EU... the U.K... and also in Japan." Chairman & CEO Dietrich added: "We're also in a process with the EU and Germany to go through a year-long qualification."

  • David Silver, Prime Executions: why Consumer & Specialties cost impact is larger? CFO Aldag: "the majority of it is energy-linked costs" with "the biggest one... transportation trucking" plus "European natural gas" and "oil derivatives, raw materials like packaging."

  • David Silver, Prime Executions: 21% sequential jump in edible oil/renewable fuel purification? Group President Monagle: "it is reasonable for you to think that is further penetration into this sustainable aviation fuel market" and "we will sustain that level of growth" while "already looking at debottlenecking and expanding further."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts slightly negative to pressing, concentrating on inflation recovery timing, segment growth durability, and commercialization cadence, including "if they do" stabilize costs, "you would expect to sort of catch up" and questions on PFAS being "a little bit below" earlier expectations. (Dan Moore, CJS Securities; David Silver, Prime Executions)

  • Management slightly positive but acknowledged near-term pressure, repeatedly emphasizing recovery actions and visibility, including "The overall cost environment continues to be volatile" and "we remain confident" on 2027 margin improvement. (CFO Aldag)

  • Versus the prior quarter, management tone shifted from broad confidence in full-year execution to sharper focus on cost volatility and contract repricing mechanics, with more explicit timing language such as "assuming costs stabilize in the first quarter" for margin normalization. (CFO Aldag)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance shifted from Q2’s "third quarter sales of approximately $550 million... operating income... around $75 million and earnings per share of between $1.55 and $1.60" (CFO Aldag, Q2 call) to Q3’s "fourth quarter sales... approximately $525 million... operating income between $60 million and $63 million and EPS between $1.15 and $1.20" and an added calendar impact: "6 fewer days" in Q4. (CFO Aldag, Q3 call)

  • Q3 introduced Investor Day reconfirmations and new quantified strategic opportunities that were not quantified in Q2 prepared remarks, including a pipeline "estimate at $1.4 billion in revenue potential," and the view that high-purity calcium could drive "over $100 million in incremental revenue" in "the next 3 to 5 years." (Chairman & CEO Dietrich)

  • Analysts’ emphasis moved from Q2’s legal/BMI reserve discussion and margin snapback timing toward Q3’s deeper probing on the cadence/capex of new growth platforms (high-purity calcium, steel slag) and the durability of Environmental & Infrastructure growth into 2027. (Q2 and Q3 Q&A)

Risks and Concerns

  • "The overall cost environment continues to be volatile with energy and transportation costs remaining near their recent peak levels." (CFO Aldag)

  • "We expect segment sales to decrease by approximately 10% sequentially" in Engineered Solutions due to "typical seasonal reduction in project activity." (CFO Aldag)

  • Residential construction demand remained weak, with Specialty Additives commentary that "Demand from residential construction customers also remained soft" and that "some of those customers have begun to communicate plans for extended shutdowns." (CFO Aldag)

  • Geopolitical and regional disruptions were cited as ongoing considerations, including "the Iran conflict continues to create some supply and export issues in the Middle East market." (Group President Argirakis)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as delivering $555 million of sales and $1.53 of EPS, with Engineered Solutions at a 17.6% operating margin while Consumer & Specialties absorbed renewed energy, transportation, and raw-material inflation. For Q4, management guided to approximately $525 million of sales and EPS of $1.15 to $1.20, highlighting six fewer days in the quarter and continued seasonal softness in Environmental & Infrastructure. Alongside near-term price-cost recovery actions—supported by efforts to "restructure the contracts" toward "more dynamic pricing models"—management elevated longer-run growth optionality at Investor Day, including an innovation pipeline estimated at $1.4 billion of revenue potential and an expected $100 million over 3 to 5 years tied to high-purity calcium metal, while advancing PFAS remediation adoption with 10 full-scale municipal drinking water installations and additional systems scheduled.

data.title: Unifi outlines $7M-$9M FY27 capex plan as it targets stronger H2 demand after asset sale
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Unifi, Inc. (UFI) Q1 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • “We reduced cost in almost every area of the company. So that work is now complete. I believe we have the necessary disciplines in place to keep our costs low.” (Executive Chairman Albert Carey)
  • “Yesterday, we closed the deal on a nonstrategic asset… Our debt is now lower than any time in recent history. Our balance sheet will be strong, and we have greater financial flexibility.” (Executive Chairman Carey)
  • “We… would have hoped these efforts would have created greater revenues by now, but the macroeconomic pressure on raw material prices has slowed down the whole industry's top-line revenue performance… we see greater demand shaping up for Q3 and Q4.” (Executive Chairman Carey)
  • “Our first quarter results continue to demonstrate the benefits of the strategic actions we've taken… This was most evident in the $9.1 million or nearly 270% increase in gross profit… and the continued improvement in cash generation.” (CEO Edmund Ingle)
  • “We recently made a great stride towards improving our balance sheet… completed sale of 2 nonstrategic real estate assets… this asset sale does not reduce our production capacity, nor will it impact our ability to service our North American customers.” (CEO Ingle)
  • “Consolidated net sales were $127.9 million… consolidated gross profit increasing to $12.5 million and gross margin expanding to 9.8%… Our net loss for the quarter came in at just $2 million… Adjusted EBITDA… was $6.1 million.” (CFO A.J. Eaker)

Outlook

  • “Our outlook and how we anticipate sustaining our financial momentum for fiscal 2027 remains unchanged… We also anticipate that our sales and profitability results will improve on a year-over-year basis as we begin to recognize the full year benefits of our past strategic actions.” (CEO Edmund Ingle)
  • “For the second quarter, we expect stable demand in the Americas segment with continued margin-accretive revenues from value-added products and Beyond Apparel initiatives.” (CEO Ingle)
  • “Our Brazil segment sales and profitability will be similar to the prior year with some working capital pressure from inflation… our Asia segment will continue to remain pressured as a result of the regional softness and geopolitical volatility.” (CEO Ingle)
  • Compared with last quarter’s positioning for fiscal 2027, management reiterated the same framework, including: “our focus will continue to remain on driving growth in margin-accretive revenues from our value-added products and Beyond Apparel initiatives” in the Americas and that Asia remained “our most challenged business segment today in terms of revenues.” (CEO Edmund Ingle, Q4 fiscal 2026)

Financial Results

  • “Consolidated net sales were $127.9 million, down 5.7%… consolidated gross profit increasing to $12.5 million and gross margin expanding to 9.8% compared to… 2.5% in the prior year period… driven by strong performance in the resin business in Brazil, our strategic repositioning efforts and portfolio management.” (CFO A.J. Eaker)
  • “In the Americas, net sales were down $8.2 million year-over-year… Despite this, we delivered our third consecutive quarter of gross profit in the Americas with gross profit reaching $4.7 million.” (CFO Eaker)
  • “Brazil… net sales increase by $4.1 million or 14.4%… driven by continued favorable pricing dynamics and improved sales mix.” (CFO Eaker)
  • “This week, we finalized the sale of 2 nonstrategic real estate assets… The proceeds were immediately used to pay down the outstanding term loan balance of $55.5 million.” (CFO Eaker)
  • “During the first quarter, we generated $2.5 million of free cash flow… CapEx for the quarter came in at just $1.2 million… we have allocated between $7 million and $9 million for the remainder of fiscal year '27.” (CFO Eaker)

Q&A

  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti & Company, LLC: asked about apparel/footwear customer signals on inventories and post-holiday replenishment; CEO Edmund Ingle answered, “we believe the inventories… they're very low… part of the reason why we're expecting… fiscal H2 to be improved… is… YarnProof… innovations… especially on the military and tactical side.”
  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti & Company, LLC: asked where Beyond Apparel demand is improving; CEO Ingle said, “we are seeing some growth in auto on the sampling side… we don't expect that growth to happen in H2… more of a fiscal 2028 volume opportunity,” and Executive Chairman Albert Carey added, “there's at least 4 customers… the work on military has led to other opportunities… Those are more Q3, Q4 kinds of outcomes.”
  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti & Company, LLC: asked for more color on the four military-linked customer relationships; Executive Chairman Carey said, “when we build a strategic partnership with a customer… You build a relationship with the top of their organization… it will be Q3 before you see that.”
  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti & Company, LLC: asked what “portfolio optimization” actions were taken; CEO Ingle said, “We have walked away from some business that was very, very challenging from a pricing point of view,” and CFO A.J. Eaker added, “we've drawn a keen eye more to what makes sense for us and the customer… And we'll continue doing that.”
  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti & Company, LLC: asked which new products management is most focused on; CEO Ingle said, “we're very excited about ThermaLoop… Fortisyn,” and added that “the A.M.Y. Peppermint program is live now, but we do expect to see that grow in the next 2 or 3 quarters.”
  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti & Company, LLC: asked when YarnProof could show financial impact; CFO Eaker said, “We expect that by mid- to late summer, all of the products in the region… will contain this tracer… expecting to see some impact in fiscal Q4 of this year and the first quarter next year,” while Executive Chairman Carey said, “this could produce results… it's tough to put your finger on it, but it definitely will make an impact.”
  • Chris Reynolds, Neuberger Berman Group LLC: pressed on why apparel demand remains “in such a deep downturn”; CEO Ingle responded, “we realize there may be a structural shift in some of the consumer patterns,” and added, “we're not relying going forward on having this come back to the same levels… We're focusing on… innovation… and do things like YarnProof.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to skeptical on core demand durability, including “I'm still struggling to figure out why the apparel business is in such a deep downturn.” (Chris Reynolds, Neuberger Berman Group LLC)
  • Management tone was slightly positive but cautious, emphasizing control levers and timing uncertainty, including “we're not relying… on having this come back to the same levels,” and “Hard to actually determine exactly how much.” (CEO Edmund Ingle; CFO A.J. Eaker)
  • Versus last quarter, management sounded more definitive on balance-sheet actions after moving from a signed agreement to closing, shifting from “we look forward to moving along with this deal” to “yesterday, we closed the deal… The proceeds were immediately used to pay down… $55.5 million.” (CEO Edmund Ingle, Q4 fiscal 2026; CFO A.J. Eaker, Q1 fiscal 2027)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Asset monetization moved from pending to completed, with Q4 describing “a purchase agreement… for… $60 million,” and Q1 stating, “we closed the deal… [and] pay down… $55.5 million.” (Executive Chairman Albert Carey; CFO A.J. Eaker)
  • The Q&A focus broadened from execution details on the asset sale (Q4) to end-market demand visibility and structural questions around apparel (Q1), including “there may be a structural shift in some of the consumer patterns.” (CEO Edmund Ingle)
  • Management’s growth narrative in Q1 leaned more heavily on compliance-driven demand catalysts, describing YarnProof as “an industry-wide initiative designed to provide immediate physical verification of… yarn origin,” versus Q4’s heavier emphasis on REPREVE platform momentum and adoption pacing. (CEO Edmund Ingle)

Risks and Concerns

  • “Geopolitical and macro uncertainty weighed on our top line this quarter.” (CEO Edmund Ingle)
  • “The escalating raw material environment caused by the rise in crude oil” required “appropriate pricing adjustments.” (CEO Ingle)
  • “Asia segment will continue to remain pressured as a result of the regional softness and geopolitical volatility.” (CEO Ingle)
  • On demand uncertainty, management flagged, “we realize there may be a structural shift in some of the consumer patterns.” (CEO Ingle)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q1 fiscal 2027 as a quarter where cost actions and portfolio changes translated into higher gross profit and improved free cash flow despite lower sales, while the completed real estate sale and immediate $55.5 million term-loan paydown was positioned as a step-change in leverage and flexibility. For the back half of the year, management pointed to low inventories, military/tactical traction, and the YarnProof supply-chain compliance program—expected to begin showing impact around fiscal Q4—as key drivers intended to convert the restructured cost base into stronger year-over-year sales and profitability momentum.

data.title: GLPI outlines 2026 guidance of $1.22B-$1.225B while funding $467M Cordish Live! Virginia project
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Gaming and Leisure Properties (GLPI) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Happy once again to report another strong quarter here at GLPI" and "our AFFO growth, again, exceeding 10% in the third quarter" (Chairman of the Board & CEO Peter Carlino).
  • "Our funding for Bally's Chicago casino remains on schedule with the casino remaining on track for a first half of 2027 opening" (Chairman of the Board & CEO Carlino).
  • "With respect to the Cordish Live! Virginia project... we will fund $467 million" and "we continue to see a healthy runway of growth from our development pipeline" (Chairman of the Board & CEO Carlino).
  • "For the third quarter of '26, our total income from real estate exceeded the third quarter of '25 by almost $38 million" (CFO & Treasurer Desiree Burke).
  • "Our leverage ratio is at 4.8x, slightly below our target level of 5 to 5.5x" and "our rent coverage ratios on our master leases range from 1.61 to 2.46x" (CFO & Treasurer Burke).

Outlook

  • "Included in our release is our full year 2026 guidance of between $1.22 billion and $1.225 billion or $4.11 to $4.12 per diluted share and OP unit" and "The guidance does not include the impact of future transactions" (CFO & Treasurer Burke).
  • "However, it does include additional development funding of approximately $265 million, bringing our total development spend for 2026 to $800 million" (CFO & Treasurer Burke).
  • "We're funding it with free cash flow and with debt for the most part because we don't like the price of our equity" (CFO & Treasurer Burke).
  • Compared with last quarter’s guidance language, management previously said 2026 development funding would be "approximately $400 million to $450 million" over "the next 2 quarters" as projects pulled capital (CFO & Treasurer Burke, Q2 2026).

Financial Results

  • "This growth was driven primarily by $47 million in increases in cash income resulting from acquisitions and escalations" while "The combination of noncash income items... results in a collective year-over-year decrease of $9.1 million" (CFO & Treasurer Burke).
  • "Our operating expenses increased by $65 million, mainly due to noncash adjustments in the provision for credit losses" (CFO & Treasurer Burke).
  • Funding and escalation contributors cited included: "The Chicago lease increased our cash income by $12 million" and "the acquisition of Bally's Lincoln real estate increased our cash income by $14 million" (CFO & Treasurer Burke).

Q&A

  • Greg McGinniss, Scotiabank: "Bally Chicago" scaling back hotel investment—does it change underwriting? President, COO & Secretary Brandon Moore: "the underwriting hasn't changed" and "when that property fully ramps, I don't think we have a different view here as to how it will perform."
  • Greg McGinniss, Scotiabank: Prologis JV funding/ownership? CFO & Treasurer Burke: "our agreement allows us... up to 30%" and "We can't tell you exactly what that will be because it depends on the opportunity and what is developed at the site."
  • James Feldman, Wells Fargo: does Prologis mean more non-gaming? SVP Corporate Strategy & IR Carlo Santarelli: "think about this as more of a one-off" and "taking advantage of an opportunity that presented itself for us."
  • Bennett Rose, Citi: buybacks and Bally’s credit? Chairman of the Board & CEO Carlino: "a buyback is always the last resort" and "So long as we can do accretive transactions... we're going to do that." SVP Corporate Strategy & IR Santarelli: "Those leases... are covered at 1.98 and 2.13x. We feel very good about that."
  • Brad Heffern, RBC: going-concern language impact? President, COO & Secretary Moore: "I don't think our overall view of their credit risk has changed" and "we feel good about the Bally's assets we have regardless of the fact that they filed this going concern 10-Q."
  • Ravi Vaidya, Mizuho: Star Entertainment fine and Bally’s exposure? SVP Corporate Strategy & IR Santarelli: "Bally's Corp. is completely unrelated to this investment" and "the Star investment has no bearing on anything that necessarily relates to us."
  • Todd Thomas, KeyBanc: equity off the table—leverage tolerance and capacity? CFO & Treasurer Burke: "When we fund all of the transactions... we'll still be at the low end of our 5 to 5.5x leverage."
  • Ronald Kamdem, Morgan Stanley: Bally Chicago construction datapoints and lease protections? SVP & Chief Development Officer Steven Ladany: "The overall project is roughly 2/3 complete" and "there are over 1,000 daily workers on site." President, COO & Secretary Moore: "we do have in our leases defaults related to their material indebtedness."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative and risk-focused around Bally’s and cost of capital, including repeated probing on "going concern" and "share repurchase program" (Bennett Rose, Citi; Brad Heffern, RBC; Ronald Kamdem, Morgan Stanley).
  • Management’s tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks but more defensive in Q&A, including "I don't think our overall view... has changed" and "Our demise has been much overexaggerated here" (President, COO & Secretary Moore).
  • Versus last quarter, management repeated a similar stance that buybacks are "always the last choice" (Chairman of the Board & CEO Carlino, Q2 2026) and again emphasized pipeline and accretive transactions over repurchases in Q3.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Management reiterated regional-gaming resilience, repeating "bulletproof" language: "the gaming revenues are bulletproof" (Chairman of the Board & CEO Carlino, Q2 2026) and "the revenues coming out of regional markets are essentially bulletproof" (Chairman of the Board & CEO Carlino, Q3 2026).
  • Q3 introduced a clearer emphasis on equity-market dislocation as a financing constraint: "triple net REIT equity valuations have been, to say the least, disappointing" (Chairman of the Board & CEO Carlino) and "we don't like the price of our equity" (CFO & Treasurer Burke).
  • The Bally’s credit discussion became more prominent in Q3, with multiple analyst questions on going-concern language and management responses centered on lease coverage and asset re-tenanting confidence.

Risks and Concerns

  • Capital markets and equity valuation risk: "despite volatility in both the debt and equity capital markets" and "triple net REIT equity valuations have been... disappointing" (Chairman of the Board & CEO Carlino).
  • Bally’s liquidity and project timing risk: "it's not something that we're excited about" (President, COO & Secretary Moore) and delays would "delay the point in time where Bally's starts to realize some cash flow" (President, COO & Secretary Moore).
  • Execution/timing risk on development: "The overall project is roughly 2/3 complete" and the casino/hotel are expected to be "weather tight by December" (SVP & Chief Development Officer Ladany).

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as another quarter of "AFFO growth... exceeding 10%" while reiterating that Bally’s Chicago remains on track for a first half of 2027 opening and that Cordish Live! Virginia underwriting is supported by temporary-facility results with GLPI funding $467 million. Executives emphasized that, amid weak REIT equity pricing, GLPI expects to rely primarily on free cash flow and debt, keeping leverage at the low end of its 5.0x–5.5x target, while maintaining focus on accretive transactions and long-term lease underwriting.

data.title: Intel plunges 29% on weak Q4 guidance
data.description:
Intel Corporation (INTC) sank almost 29% on Friday after the semiconductor giant's fourth-quarter guidance came in well below Wall Street expectations, overshadowing a solid third-quarter beat.

Shares ended at $65.76, down $26.31 from the prior close. Volume surged to nearly 399 million shares, more than four times the one-month average. INTC has fallen nearly 45% in the past month.

The selloff contributed to a broad technology-sector decline, with the Nasdaq-tracking QQQ falling more than 3% and the technology sector ETF sliding nearly 5%. Intel's semiconductor peers also fell sharply: AMD dropped just over 11%, TSM slid just over 6%, AVGO shed more than 5%, MU declined almost 6%, and NVDA fell just over 4%.

Intel reported third-quarter non-GAAP EPS of $0.52, beating estimates by $0.12, and revenue of $16.51 billion, edging past consensus by $20 million. Data-center and AI revenue reached $7.3 billion, nearly 80% higher year over year, and management said server demand remained strong. Read more

Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $0.25 fell short of consensus, as management flagged three concurrent headwinds, including an industry-wide shortage of advanced substrates and what management described as an unprecedented memory crunch.

data.title: Bank of America sued over mandatory arbitration policy for employees
data.description:
Bank of America (BAC) has been sued by a fired financial adviser over its mandatory arbitration policy for employees, Reuters reported on Friday.

Katherine Mackey has challenged the bank's 2024 policy that requires BofA and Merrill Lynch employees to accept ​mandatory arbitration through JAMS for several claims instead of litigation, the report noted.

Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services, or JAMS, is a private alternative dispute resolution provider.

Mackey's complaint reportedly said she joined a Merrill Lynch program for aspiring financial advisers in 2023, where she was subjected ⁠to discrimination and harassment because of her gender and age.

She wants to void the arbitration policy so she can move her claims to federal court from arbitration, where she filed as a ⁠precaution, according to the newswire.

According to Mackey, the policy negated BofA's $160M settlement in a lawsuit in August 2013 on gender discrimination.

"Congress and the ​Supreme Court have long encouraged the use of arbitration to resolve employment disputes," a BofA spokesperson reportedly said. "Arbitration ⁠policies using JAMS as the forum for arbitration are routinely upheld in court, as has this one."
